newsitem.title: UK: LIMIT seen making Bankside offer shortly.
newsitem.headline: LIMIT seen making Bankside offer shortly.

text.p: The biggest corporate investor in Lloyd's of London is likely to press ahead with a formal offer for one of the insurance market's underwriting agents.
LIMIT is expected shortly to post a formal offer document to shareholders in Bankside following their approval this month to demerge the underwriting agent's associated members' agency.
Analysts said the offer document, which will provide by way of a cash offer to certain shareholders an estimate of how much LIMIT thinks Bankside is worth, could come later next week.

Bankside manages eight Lloyd's insurance syndicates with a total capacity of 403 million stg. Capacity is how much business the market can underwrite in terms of premium income. Lloyd's total for this year was around 10 billion stg. LIMIT (London Insurance Market Investment Trust) declared in August its intention to buy two Lloyd's underwriting agencies -- Janson Green and Bankside. The 18.6 million stg takeover of Janson Green went unconditional last month.
